subject: maths
title: Adding and Subtracting 2-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Year 2 Adding and Subtracting 2-Digit Numbers Worksheets: Tens and Ones, Number Lines and Word Problems
standard_text: Add and subtract numbers using concrete objects, pictorial representations, and mentally, including: a two-digit number and ones; a two-digit number and tens; two two-digit numbers; adding three one-digit numbers; solve problems with addition and subtraction.
meta_desc: Free Year 2 maths worksheets on adding and subtracting 2-digit numbers: add and subtract ones and tens, cross a ten, add two 2-digit numbers, add three 1-digit numbers and solve word problems with tens and ones pictures and number lines. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the National Curriculum.
key_big: Add the tens to the tens and the ones to the ones.
key_sub: 34 + 20 = 54 and 34 + 5 = 39. If the ones go past 10, cross to the next ten: 47 + 6 = 53.
body_html:
Tens and ones

A 2-digit number is made of tens and ones. 47 is 4 tens and 7 ones. Add ones to the ones. Add tens to the tens.

CalculationAnswerWhat changes
42 + 547the ones: 2 + 5 = 7
42 + 3072the tens: 4 + 3 = 7
68 − 464the ones: 8 − 4 = 4
68 − 2048the tens: 6 − 2 = 4

Crossing a ten

Sometimes the ones go past 10. Jump to the next ten first. Then add the rest.

Example

What is 52 − 7?

Jump back 2 to the ten: 52 − 2 = 50. 7 is 2 + 5, so take away 5 more: 50 − 5 = 45.

Answer: 45

Adding two 2-digit numbers

Add the tens. Then add the ones. If there are 10 or more ones, exchange 10 ones for 1 ten.

Example

What is 35 + 42?

Tens: 30 + 40 = 70. Ones: 5 + 2 = 7. 70 + 7 = 77.

Answer: 77

Subtracting with an exchange

If there are not enough ones, exchange 1 ten for 10 ones.

Adding three numbers

You can add numbers in any order. Look for a number bond to 10 first.

Check with the inverse

Subtraction undoes addition. If 47 + 38 = 85, then 85 − 38 = 47.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding ones to the tens: 47 + 6 = 1076 is 6 ones. Add it to the ones: 53
Not crossing the ten: 47 + 6 = 437 + 6 = 13, so the tens go up by 1: 53
Adding tens to the ones: 34 + 20 = 3620 is 2 tens. Add it to the tens: 54
Taking the smaller digit from the larger: 63 − 28 = 45Exchange 1 ten for 10 ones: 13 − 8 = 5. Answer: 35

faq.q: What addition and subtraction should a Year 2 child know?
faq.a: The National Curriculum says Year 2 children should add and subtract a two-digit number and ones, a two-digit number and tens, two two-digit numbers, and three one-digit numbers, using objects, pictures and mental methods.

faq.q: How do Year 2 children add two 2-digit numbers?
faq.a: They partition the numbers into tens and ones. For 35 + 42, add the tens (30 + 40 = 70), then the ones (5 + 2 = 7), to get 77. Tens and ones blocks and number lines help.

faq.q: Do Year 2 children learn column addition?
faq.a: Formal column addition and subtraction are taught in Year 3. In Year 2, children use tens and ones blocks, number lines and partitioning, which prepare them for columns.

faq.q: How do you add three one-digit numbers?
faq.a: Look for two numbers that make 10, or a double, and add those first. For 7 + 5 + 3, add 7 + 3 = 10, then 10 + 5 = 15.

items.q: Use the blocks. What is 34 + 20?
items.e: 20 is 2 tens. Add the tens: 3 tens + 2 tens = 5 tens. The ones stay the same. 34 + 20 = 54.

items.q: The blocks show 76. 3 tens are crossed out. What is 76 − 30?
items.e: 30 is 3 tens. Take away the tens: 7 tens − 3 tens = 4 tens. The ones stay the same. 76 − 30 = 46.

items.q: Count on in tens. What is 45 + 30?
items.e: Count on 3 tens from 45: 55, 65, 75. The ones stay the same. 45 + 30 = 75.

items.q: Count back in tens. What is 82 − 40?
items.e: Count back 4 tens from 82: 72, 62, 52, 42. The ones stay the same. 82 − 40 = 42.
10 more means 1 more ten. 5 tens become 6 tens. The ones stay the same: 67.
10 less means 1 fewer ten. 6 tens become 5 tens. The ones stay the same: 53.

items.e: 30 is 3 tens, so only the tens digit changes: 24 + 30 = 54.

items.q: Take away the tens, then the ones. What is 63 − 28?
items.e: Take away the tens first: 63 − 20 = 43. Then take away 8. Go back to the ten: 43 − 3 = 40, then 40 − 5 = 35.

items.e: Tens: 4 + 3 = 7 tens. Ones: 7 + 8 = 15 ones. Exchange 10 ones for 1 ten: 8 tens and 5 ones. 47 + 38 = 85.

items.q: Add 20, then take away 1. What is 46 + 19?
items.e: 19 is 1 less than 20. 46 + 20 = 66. Then 66 − 1 = 65. (66 forgets to take away 1.)
Subtraction undoes addition. Start at 85 and take away 38: 85 − 38 = 47.
You can add in any order: 42 + 35 is also 77. You cannot swap the numbers in a subtraction.

items.q: There are 34 books on a shelf. Kai puts 5 more books on the shelf. How many books are on the shelf now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Add the ones: 4 + 5 = 9. The tens stay the same. 34 + 5 = 39.

items.q: Alfie has 46 marbles. He wins 7 more marbles. How many marbles does he have now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Make the next ten first. 46 + 4 = 50. 7 is 4 + 3, so add 3 more: 50 + 3 = 53.

items.q: A bus has 52 people on it. 8 people get off. How many people are still on the bus?
items.e: Some get off, so subtract. Go back to the ten first. 52 − 2 = 50. 8 is 2 + 6, so take away 6 more: 50 − 6 = 44.

items.q: There are 26 ducks on a pond. 9 more ducks land. How many ducks are there now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Make the next ten first. 26 + 4 = 30. 9 is 4 + 5, so add 5 more: 30 + 5 = 35.

items.q: Ruby has 63 stickers. She gives 30 stickers to her friend. How many stickers does she have left?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 30 is 3 tens. Take away the tens: 6 tens − 3 tens = 3 tens. The ones stay the same. 63 − 30 = 33.

items.q: One bus has 24 children on it. Another bus has 30 children. How many children are there altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. 30 is 3 tens. Add the tens: 2 tens + 3 tens = 5 tens. The ones stay the same. 24 + 30 = 54.

items.q: There are 81 children in the playground. 40 children go in for lunch. How many children are still in the playground?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 40 is 4 tens. Take away the tens: 8 tens − 4 tens = 4 tens. The ones stay the same. 81 − 40 = 41.

items.q: Arjun has 7 red pencils, 5 blue pencils and 3 green pencils. How many pencils does he have?
items.e: Add all three numbers. Look for a number bond to 10: 7 + 3 = 10. Then 10 + 5 = 15.

items.q: In a game, Noah scores 6 points, then 8 points, then 4 points. How many points does he score altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Look for a number bond to 10: 6 + 4 = 10. Then 10 + 8 = 18.

items.q: Aisha reads 35 pages on Monday and 42 pages on Tuesday. How many pages does she read altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Add the tens: 30 + 40 = 70. Add the ones: 5 + 2 = 7. Then 70 + 7 = 77.

items.q: A farmer has 47 sheep in one field and 38 sheep in another field. How many sheep are there altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Add the tens: 40 + 30 = 70. Add the ones: 7 + 8 = 15. Then 70 + 15 = 85.

items.q: A shop has 72 apples. It sells 25 apples. How many apples are left?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. Take away the tens first: 72 − 20 = 52. Then take away 5. Go back to the ten: 52 − 2 = 50, then 50 − 3 = 47.

items.q: A bus has 40 seats. 26 people are sitting down. How many seats are empty?
items.e: Take the seats with people away from all the seats, so subtract. Take away the tens first: 40 − 20 = 20. Then take away the ones: 20 − 6 = 14.

items.q: Zara has 45 marbles. Amelia has 28 marbles. How many more marbles does Zara have than Amelia?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. Take away the tens first: 45 − 20 = 25. Then take away 8. Go back to the ten: 25 − 5 = 20, then 20 − 3 = 17.

items.q: A pencil costs 45p. A rubber costs 38p. Evie buys both. How much does she spend?
items.e: Buying both means add. Add the tens: 40 + 30 = 70. Add the ones: 5 + 8 = 13. Then 70 + 13 = 83. So the answer is 83p.

items.q: Harry has 75p. He spends 30p on a drink. How much money does he have left?
items.e: Spending means subtract. 30 is 3 tens. Take away the tens: 7 tens − 3 tens = 4 tens. The ones stay the same. 75 − 30 = 45. So the answer is 45p.

items.q: An ice lolly costs 35p. Ava pays with a £1 coin. How much change does she get?
items.e: £1 is 100p. Count on from 35p to 100p: 35p + 5p = 40p, then 40p + 60p = 100p. 5p + 60p = 65p.

items.q: Ethan has a 50p coin, a 20p coin and a 5p coin. How much money does he have?
items.e: Add all three coins: 50p + 20p = 70p, then 70p + 5p = 75p.

items.q: There are 45 people on a bus. 8 people get off. Then 20 people get on. How many people are on the bus now?
Maya has 58 beads. Lily has 9 fewer beads than Maya. How many beads does Lily have?
items.e: Fewer means subtract. 58 − 8 = 50, then 50 − 1 = 49.
